title: Tricky Tactics Auto Warranty (Telemarketing)
summary: A news report on a telemarketer who pressured an elderly woman into paying for an auto warranty service contract over the phone.

assertions.quote: Your auto warranty is expired or will expire shortly
it was nowhere near what it was they were expecting based on the phone call

verdicts.note: Reported directly by postal inspectors and victims in the segment.

FTC says scam service contracts can carry "so many limits and conditions on which repairs are covered... that the service contract is worthless," consistent with buyers getting far less than pitched, though the guide doesn't quantify the gap versus the phone pitch.

CarShield's telemarketers pitched specific terms (e.g. a flat $100 deductible for any covered repair, all repairs covered), but the FTC found the coverage actually sold was far more limited, with many exclusions, denials and shops that wouldn't accept the plan.
